## LCSC verification

- Date: 24 Nov 2026. Every line with a part carries an LCSC number (column LCSC); PCB features are `n/a`.
- How: lcsc.com product-detail JSON (wmsc.lcsc.com/ftps/wm/product/detail?productCode=C...) per part: MPN, manufacturer, package, description/parameters, stock, price ladder; candidates found with the jlcpcb.com parts search (same data source); JLC library type and stock from that search. Checked per part: MPN, value, tolerance, dielectric / voltage rating, package against the board footprint, LCSC stock (column Stock) and the price at the ladder step nearest 10 pcs (column P~10).
- Generic passives: UNI-ROYAL 0402WGF 1 % thick film, 0.1 % 25 ppm/K thin film (YAGEO RT0402BRD07 where stocked), FH / Murata / KEMET C0G, Samsung / FH X5R-X7R; one number per value / package / rating (`kicad/gen/common.py`).
- Not on LCSC: J501 Würth 490107671612 (footprint only (Würth Redfit IDC, yanartas J3 pinout), no part; not on LCSC: RS 197-3364).

## If the budget gets tight: cheapest cuts

The board is under budget; these are the options in order of cost per USD saved, should prices move:

1. **SMA connectors** (2 x 4.68, Samtec SMA-J-P-H-ST-EM1 C5199907): generic LCSC edge-launch SMAs are 0.5-2.0 (the RF Solutions CON-SMA-EDGE-S C5356059 was out of stock on 24 Nov 2026); saves up to ~8, but needs a footprint check (1.6 mm board fit, >3 GHz rating).
2. **GVA-84+ -> TRF37D73** in the phase-strobe chains: saves ~3, but sim/strobe/RESULT.md gives only 2.15 V per line (below the 2.75 V the taps need with the 80 ps stub). Not recommended.
3. **TLV3801 -> TLV3601** (single-ended output): saves ~0.5, needs a redesign of the LVDS split. Not worth it.
4. **50k trimmer -> fixed 33.2k** (RV101): saves ~0.5 if the VOFS/LF-gain trim is done in software.
5. **300k / 280k 0.1 %** (R114-R116, R613, R605: 0.37-0.38 each, low-stock Vishay / TE parts): a 0.1 % 50 ppm/K or 0.5 % part would save ~1.5.
